:::{#thm-modus-tollens}
#### Modus tollens

For [propositions](#def-proposition) $P$ and $Q$,
this is a [rule of inference](#def-rule-of-inference):

$$
\frac{P \Rightarrow Q, \quad \neg Q}{\neg P}
$$

:::

::: proof

Suppose both [premises](#def-premise) are true.
By the definition of [not](#def-not),
$Q$ is false.
By the definition of [implies](#def-implies),
a true $P \Rightarrow Q$ with a false $Q$ needs a false $P$.
So $P$ is false,
and the [conclusion](#def-conclusion) $\neg P$ is true.

:::
